text:
ravi: FYI eu-central1 saw a small spike in GPU attach failures ~00:10Z. Pods stuck at ContainerCreating ~90s.

emma: any obvious network blips?

ravi: network fine. iostat shows nvme queue depth and small write bursts at scrub start. snippet:
```
nvme0n1 r/s=30 w/s=340 avgqusz=19 await=38ms %util=84
```

storage-bot: ALERT ephemeral-cleaner iops_spike eu-central1 2026-03-19T00:12Z p99=95ms

niall: probably the cleaner sweep colliding with nightly model-cache warmups. Two heavy IO jobs starting at same time.

emma: short term: reduce cleaner batch size and stagger start windows. We have `cleaner.batch` in config. Set to 1 and add node label start-offset.

ravi: I'll push config to canary nodes: `cfg set cleaner.batch 1 && cfg reload`. Also running small script to label nodes janitor-offset=0..4m.

ops-bot: ACTION applied to eu-central1-canary 2026-03-19T00:18Z

niall: canary saw util drop 84% -> 48% and attach failures -> 0.8% within 45s.

emma: rolling to region with 30s stagger windows. Note: longer scrub duration, cost +0.6% estimate. Communicating to CS.

ravi: created ticket INFRA-4410, will add graphs and follow-up RFC for a "scrub-shepherd" coordinator that uses persistent cursors so restarts don't rewalk directories.

niall: followup todo: expose per-region throttle knob in platform-config and add runbook step to throttle via svc if spikes recur.

emma: leaving monitoring on for 2h. If stable, revert batch to default next maintenance window but keep stagger labels for the week.

ravi: thanks all, closing thread once graphs are attached. :thumbsup:
